prompt_payload.task: Design a diverse library of executable semantic optimization skills for finite-pool scientific search. Each skill defines interpretable rule features plus a conservative Bayesian linear surrogate blended with strong target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI anchors.

target.title: MoleculeNet Lipophilicity replay
target.boundary: Field values and counts are public; target outcomes are not included.

source_transfer_evidence.boundary: No source identity, source schema, source outcomes, source effects, or source value priors are provided. The LLM must use the public target schema and its pretrained domain knowledge only.

executor.semantic_model: Rules become binary features. Revealed target outcomes fit a ridge Bayesian linear surrogate whose coefficient prior follows rule weights.
executor.anchor: A rank blend of target-only GP-UCB and GP-EI.
executor.fusion: semantic_mass_start/end controls the rank mass assigned to the semantic surrogate; the remaining mass stays on the target-only anchor.
executor.selection: Independent calibration seeds select one frozen skill. Independent held-out seeds are evaluated only after selection.

design_requirements: Use only exact field/value pairs in public_semantic_fields.

Each conditions object must map a real catalog field name directly to one exact catalog value, for example {"dominant_family": "oxide"}. Never use literal placeholder keys such as exact_field, field_name, field, or value.
Give every skill a distinct, descriptive scientific skill_id. Never copy schema placeholders such as short_unique_name or add numeric suffixes to a placeholder.
Give every skill 3-10 rules; use two-condition interactions only when scientifically meaningful.
Include at least one conservative low-semantic-mass skill.
Use only target-schema-compatible domain knowledge; do not imply that a source task or source outcomes were observed.
Include at least one domain-knowledge skill.
Include a counter-hypothesis skill that reverses or downweights an uncertain source relation.
Prefer mechanistic, chemically or physically interpretable rules over arbitrary coverage rules.
Use positive weights for conditions expected to improve the target objective and negative weights for risks.
Do not claim access to target outcomes and do not output candidate identifiers.

rules.rationale: short scientific rationale

skills.hypothesis: what this skill transfers and when it may fail

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: real_suzuki_miyaura to real_buchwald_hartwig
cards.summary: All evidence modes failed calibration and fell back to the target acquisition portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: target_only_schema to real_matbench_log_kvrh
cards.summary: No LLM strategy passed calibration; the selected GP-EI anchor did not beat the held-out target portfolio.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Gate-rejected transfer: source_schema_only to real_chemlex_acidamine
cards.summary: The router selected GP-UCB; the descriptive held-out strongest target portfolio remained higher on the 20-seed development range.
cards.content: Reusable lesson: do not force a source-derived semantic policy when every evidence mode fails calibration. Preserve the target-only fallback and improve the reaction representation before retrying.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: counter_hypothesis_low_hbond_donors
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_esol, use the LLM to define the counter_hypothesis_low_hbond_donors feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: target_calibrated. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

cards.title: Reusable semantic feature pattern: high_aromatic_content
cards.summary: For real_moleculenet_lipophilicity, use the LLM to define the high_aromatic_content feature partition, then fit its direction and magnitude from revealed target observations.
cards.content: Evidence mode: target_only. Execution: disabled. Reusable lesson: preserve the LLM-proposed feature partition, but calibrate or remove unsupported coefficient signs before held-out evaluation.

care_knowledge_context.instruction: Use these public, previously archived cards only as reusable design lessons. Do not copy reported target values into a rule and do not imply that the current target outcomes were observed. Prefer lessons that survived held-out calibration.

rules.rationale: High aromatic content increases hydrophobicity and enhances lipophilicity.
Moderate heteroatom presence can balance polarity without overly reducing lipophilicity.
Absence of halogens may reduce hydrophobic contributions, slightly lowering lipophilicity.
High ring token count correlates with rigid, hydrophobic molecular frameworks.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the principle that aromaticity and ring structures enhance lipophilicity; may fail for highly polar or charged aromatic systems.

rules.rationale: High halogen content significantly increases hydrophobicity and lipophilicity.
Moderate branching can enhance molecular volume and hydrophobic surface area.
Low double bond count reduces polarity, favoring lipophilicity.
Low heteroatom presence may limit hydrophobic interactions if overly simple.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the known hydrophobic effect of halogens; may fail for molecules with countervailing polar groups or conformational issues.

rules.rationale: Moderate aromaticity provides a baseline hydrophobic contribution.
High heteroatom content increases polarity, likely reducing lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers minimal semantic assumptions, heavily relying on the GP anchor; may fail if simple rules miss complex lipophilicity drivers.

rules.rationale: Low heteroatom count minimizes polarity, favoring higher lipophilicity.
Moderate halogenation adds hydrophobicity without excessive molecular weight.
Low aromaticity may reduce hydrophobic character, lowering lipophilicity.
High branching increases molecular volume, potentially enhancing lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the principle that low polarity enhances lipophilicity; may fail for molecules where specific polar groups participate in hydrophobic interactions.

rules.rationale: Combination of high ring count and moderate branching optimizes rigidity and hydrophobic surface area.
Low halogen presence avoids potential toxicity while maintaining some hydrophobicity.
Moderate double bonds contribute to planarity without excessive polarity.
Moderate aromaticity supports hydrophobic pi-stacking interactions.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the synergistic effect of ring structures and branching on lipophilicity; may fail for overly flexible or polar ring systems.

rules.rationale: Absence of halogens may indicate other hydrophobic groups, avoiding halogen-specific liabilities.
High heteroatom content could involve hydrophobic heterocycles, potentially increasing lipophilicity.
Low aromaticity may favor aliphatic hydrophobicity, which can be significant.
High double bond count increases polarity and planarity, potentially reducing lipophilicity.

skills.hypothesis: Counters the typical halogen-dependence hypothesis; may fail if halogens are indeed critical for lipophilicity in this dataset.

rules.rationale: No heteroatoms likely indicate simple hydrocarbons, which may have lower than expected lipophilicity due to lack of functional group interactions.
High aromaticity with low halogenation balances hydrophobicity and avoids excessive molecular weight.
Moderate ring token count indicates optimal molecular rigidity for membrane partitioning.
Low branching may reduce hydrophobic surface area, lowering lipophilicity.
No double bonds minimizes polarity, favoring lipophilicity in saturated systems.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers domain knowledge about polar surface area and molecular rigidity; may fail for molecules where specific polar groups enhance lipophilicity through unconventional mechanisms.

rules.rationale: Mid-length SMILES indicate moderate molecular size, often optimal for lipophilicity.
Balanced heteroatom and halogen content provides hydrophobicity without excessive polarity.
Moderate aromaticity and ring count synergize for stable hydrophobic character.
High branching with low double bonds maximizes aliphatic hydrophobicity.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the principle of balanced molecular complexity for lipophilicity; may fail for molecules where extreme values in one feature dominate.
